name: Akatsuki
first: Recovered from a 5-year solar-orbit hold to achieve Venus orbit on a backup attempt; currently the only active Venus orbiter
description: Akatsuki — "dawn" — was Japan's first Venus mission. Launched 2010-05-20 from Tanegashima on an H-IIA 202, paired with the IKAROS solar-sail demonstrator. The planned Venus orbit insertion 2010-12-07 failed when salt crystal buildup in an oxidiser check valve threw the main engine off-axis 152 seconds into the burn. JAXA kept the spacecraft alive in solar orbit for five years, twelve correction maneuvers, until the next Venus encounter window. On 2015-12-07 a 1228-second burn using four attitude-control thrusters — never designed for orbital insertion — placed Akatsuki into a highly elliptical 400 × 440,000 km, 3°-inclination orbit. One of the most dramatic mission-saves in spaceflight history. Still active.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: H-IIA 202 from Tanegashima, paired with IKAROS solar sail.

events.label: VOI-1 FAILURE
events.note: 2010-12-07. OME throttle anomaly 152s into the burn; spacecraft sails past into solar orbit.

events.label: SOLAR-ORBIT HOLD
events.note: 12 maneuvers over 5 years to maintain a Venus re-encounter trajectory.

events.label: SCIENCE OPERATIONS
events.note: UV/IR cloud-feature tracking; super-rotation studies; bow-shaped gravity waves above Aphrodite Terra.
